key_insight: A readily available smartphone can provide low-cost mechanical excitation for ultrasound elastography, with preliminary phantom reconstructions similar to those obtained using a dedicated actuator.
engineering_relevance: Smartphone-based excitation could reduce hardware costs and integration complexity for tissue stiffness imaging.
method: Use a smartphone to induce mechanical displacements in a tissue-mimicking phantom.
Image the phantom response with ultrasound.
Solve the elasticity inverse problem using a finite element method.
evidence_signal: Preliminary phantom experiments yielded elasticity reconstructions similar to those produced with dedicated-actuator harmonic excitation, but the abstract reports no quantitative accuracy metrics.
watch_item: Feasibility is demonstrated only in a phantom; excitation reproducibility and clinical performance remain unestablished.
paper_title: Ultrasound Elastography: Excitation Methods and Low-Cost Alternative
